findings.evidence: `quotientSubobject_ker_eq_mk` at line 129 and `exists_surjective_hopf_presentation` at line 206 are private, while the only public inverse lemma at line 284 applies when the subgroup is already written as `quotientClosedSubgroup H I`.
findings.fix: Expose a theorem computing `(hopfIdealOrderIsoClosedSubgroup H).symm P` as `HopfIdeal.ker f.hom hf` under the `e`, `f`, and spectrum-factorization hypotheses, or expose the underlying quotient-subobject characterization needed to derive it.
findings.issue: The inverse is characterized only on `quotientClosedSubgroup`; users cannot show that an explicitly presented closed subgroup maps to the kernel of its surjective coordinate morphism without reproducing the private presentation proof.

findings.evidence: The file defines `mono_of_isClosedImmersion_underlying` at line 59, but it consumes a typeclass instance; the explicit `hi` argument at line 89 is not available to synthesize the preceding `[Mono i]` argument.
findings.fix: Remove the `[Mono i]` parameter and install the mono instance inside `mk` from `hi` (or take closed immersion as a typeclass parameter so the existing instance can synthesize `Mono i`). Update `coe_mk` similarly.
findings.issue: `ClosedSubgroupScheme.mk` requires `[Mono i]` separately even though its explicit `hi : IsClosedImmersion ...` mathematically and internally suffices to obtain `Mono i`, making the advertised constructor unusable from a closed-immersion proof alone.

summary: The classification’s inverse lacks the characteristic lemma needed to compute it from an explicit closed-subgroup presentation, and the general constructor unnecessarily requires callers to supply a separate `Mono` instance.
